assessment: Placental mesenchymal stromal cells (pMSCs) are of interest in therapeutic applications. These cells are typically generated by culturing cells isolated from the villous core of the placenta. However, the villous core is comprised of multiple cell types and the heterogeneity of these cells is often not considered. Consequently, the origin of pMSCs under commonly used culture conditions remains unclear. In the present study the authors have used sophisticated flow cytometry analysis to characterize the heterogeneity of subtypes in the placental villus core in the first trimester of gestation and present convincing data that a specific subpopulation identified likely corresponds to pMSCs in culture generated using standard isolation protocols. This study will be valuable to scientists investigating the use of placental mesenchymal stromal cells in a therapeutic context.
